speech.title: Maslenitsa
speech.text: Maslenitsa is one of the oldest and most cheerful Russian holidays. It is celebrated during the last week before Lent and marks the end of winter and the coming of spring. The main symbol of the holiday is the pancake, or blin: round, golden and warm, it reminds people of the sun. During Maslenitsa week families visit each other, eat pancakes with sour cream, honey or caviar and take part in outdoor fun. In many towns people ride in sledges, have snowball fights and organise competitions. On the last day, known as Forgiveness Sunday, people ask one another for forgiveness, and a large straw figure of Lady Maslenitsa is burnt to say goodbye to winter.

speech.title: The Hermitage
speech.text: The State Hermitage in St Petersburg is one of the largest and oldest museums in the world. It was founded in 1764 by Catherine the Great, who bought a collection of paintings from a merchant in Berlin. At first the collection was private, and only the empress and her guests could see it. The museum was opened to the public in 1852. Today the Hermitage occupies several historic buildings, including the magnificent Winter Palace, the former residence of the Russian tsars. Its collection includes over three million items, from ancient Egyptian objects to works by Leonardo da Vinci, Rembrandt and Picasso. It is said that if you spent just one minute looking at each exhibit, it would take you many years to see them all.

speech.title: Yuri Gagarin
speech.text: On 12 April 1961 Yuri Gagarin became the first person to travel into space. His spacecraft, Vostok 1, orbited the Earth once, and the whole flight lasted just 108 minutes. Gagarin was born in 1934 in a small village in the Smolensk region. As a young man he studied at an industrial college, joined a flying club and later became a military pilot. He was chosen for the space programme from many candidates because of his calm character, quick reactions and excellent health. After his historic flight, Gagarin became a hero not only in his own country but all over the world. Today 12 April is celebrated in Russia as Cosmonautics Day, and many streets, schools and even a crater on the Moon are named after him.

speech.title: Dmitri Mendeleev
speech.text: Dmitri Mendeleev was one of the greatest chemists in history. In 1869 he created the periodic table, a system that arranged all the chemical elements known at that time according to their properties. What made his work truly brilliant was that he left empty spaces in the table for elements that had not yet been discovered. He even predicted what these elements would be like. In the years that followed, scientists found three of them — gallium, scandium and germanium — and their properties matched his predictions remarkably well. Mendeleev was also interested in many other fields, from oil production to shipbuilding. Today the element mendelevium is named after him, and his table hangs in almost every school classroom in the world.

speech.title: The Russian dacha
speech.text: For many Russian families, the dacha is much more than a country house. It is a place where people escape from the noise of the city, breathe fresh air and spend time with their relatives. Most dachas are small wooden houses with a garden, where families grow potatoes, cucumbers, tomatoes and berries. In summer, city dwellers travel there every weekend, and children often spend the whole holiday there with their grandparents. Life at the dacha has its own traditions: making jam from home-grown berries, heating the banya on Saturday evening and having long conversations over a cup of tea. Even today, when supermarkets sell everything all year round, millions of Russians still love working in their gardens.

reading11.title: Russia: a country of contrasts
reading11.text:
Russia is the largest country in the world, and it stretches from the Baltic Sea in the west {A}. Because of its size, the country has an enormous variety of landscapes and climates.
In the north, where winters are long and harsh, the land is covered with tundra and taiga, {B}. The south, by contrast, has a mild climate, and people can enjoy the warm beaches of the Black Sea.
Russia is also rich in cultural heritage. Its cities boast magnificent cathedrals, palaces and museums {C}. Many of these sights are listed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
The country is home to more than 190 ethnic groups, {D}. That is why Russian cuisine, traditions and holidays are so diverse.
Russians are proud of their history and {E}: Mendeleev's periodic table, the first artificial satellite and Yuri Gagarin's flight. {F}, Russia remains one of the most fascinating countries to explore.
